blindSummary: A 2023 law makes refusing to leave a facility not matching sex assigned at birth - after being told by a government employee - criminal trespass in state-owned buildings. It produced what is believed to be the first arrest anywhere under a state transgender bathroom law (March 2025, at the legislature complex; held about 24 hours; charges later dismissed on a technicality). The state/province stopped issuing corrected-marker licences and treats "misrepresentation" as potential fraud; a state LGBTQ equality organisation and the country's largest LGBTQ advocacy group issued travel advisories naming this state/province. Recorded lethal violence is lower than the statutes suggest: 3.7 killings per 100k trans women/yr, below the average of the country's most heavily banning states/provinces.
blindSourceSummaries: The state's civil-liberties union know-your-rights page (updated March 2024) explaining the 2023 facilities law: refusing to leave a restroom or changing facility not matching sex assigned at birth, after being told to by a government employee, is criminal trespass in state-owned buildings; the page calls the law 'complex, confusing, and vague' and lays out its limited actual coverage (multi-user facilities in government buildings).

National broadcaster and wire-service report (April 2025): a 20-year-old trans woman was arrested on 19 March 2025 after using a women's restroom in the state/province legislature - believed by civil-rights attorneys to be the first arrest anywhere under a state transgender bathroom criminal ban; a second-degree misdemeanour trespass charge carrying up to 60 days. The report notes that of at least 14 states/provinces with bathroom restrictions, only this state/province and one other criminalise the act itself.

An LGBTQ news outlet (July 2025): a county judge dismissed the trespass charges on 20 June 2025 on speedy-trial grounds after the state failed to file charging documents within 90 days; because she was charged with trespass rather than under a separate 2023 facilities law, she could not challenge the bathroom ban's constitutionality in the case.

A state LGBTQ equality organisation's press release (11 April 2023): a sub-national travel advisory warning of risks to the health, safety and freedom of people travelling to or relocating to this state/province, issued in response to laws the organisation calls hostile to the LGBTQ community; the country's largest LGBTQ advocacy group joined with an updated advisory in 2024. One of only a few named sub-national travel advisories of its kind in the country.

An independent data-journalism outlet's state-by-state analysis (July 2026) overlaying legal-risk maps on recorded trans-homicide data: legal risk predicts how the state treats you, not how people do; this state/province's recorded killing rate for trans women is 3.7 per 100k/yr, below the average of the most heavily banning states/provinces - and all counts are floors from an acknowledged undercount.
blindOutOfScope: The travel advisory itself also cites non-trans laws (reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety repeals, curriculum censorship); those shape the general rights climate but do not move trans-specific visitor risk.
blindTangential: Pride and civic visibility are being rolled back across the state/province - removal of Pride crosswalks, with residents of one large city defying the state - visibility conflicts affecting LGBT+ presence broadly rather than trans status specifically.
